- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.7) — reduce forecast peak by 2–5%.
- Underestimate prices after strong upward spikes — add 1–3% to forecast to avoid “overshoot” lag.
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly bearish (0.2–0.5), model tends to overreact — dampen forecast volatility.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–3%.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid overconfidence in early forecast days — especially if sentiment is rising — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for first 5 days.
- If sentiment is trending upward but price is flat or falling, model overestimates — reduce forecast by 1–2%.
- If sentiment is high but price is trending down, model overcorrects — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid “sentiment reversal” lag.
